title: NDH payer endpoint and organization coverage
headline: Of 114,071 FHIR REST endpoints in the 2026-05-08 NDH release, 1 (0.0009%) is a payer provider directory, and no payer organization type exists across 1,999,818 typed Organization resources. The NDH does not yet function as a payer-endpoint discovery index.
notes:
Organization.type carries exactly three codings in this release: prov (Healthcare Provider), team, govt. There is no payer type, so payer organizations cannot be selected by type. Name matching is not a substitute: every Pennsylvania organization matching payer-like name patterns is in fact a provider (KEYSTONE RURAL HEALTH CENTER and similar), which is why this check classifies by endpoint host rather than organization name.

Where payer endpoints are carried, they are largely unusable as an index: of the 92 payer-host endpoints found, 7 carry a managingOrganization reference, so the endpoint cannot be resolved to an organization for the rest. Status mix: active=62, error=30.

The provider-directory count is a floor, not a census: it counts servers that self-label in their URL path. A directory hosted at an unlabelled path is not counted, so the true number may be higher. The control probe is what makes the gap concrete, by taking a directory verified live and unauthenticated and checking whether the index knows it.

This measures a release, not compliance. Payer endpoint coverage has been discussed in the NDH community as intended direction; what is reported here is the distance between that direction and the shipped file, which is the actionable part.
